newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Prime says 4-month earnings up 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Prime says 4-month earnings up 10 pct.

text.p: Regional television broadcaster Prime Television Ltd said on Tuesday its earnings before tax and after interest for the four months to October 31 had risen 10.2 percent.

"We have been operating in a relatively flat advertising market, but the inclusion of the Olympics programming and because we have been doing better than our competition in the past few months has meant that our net earnings before tax have risen 10.2 percent in the first four months of 1996/97," Prime's managing director George Brown told the annual meeting.
Brown said the company expected to achieve earnings close to budget in November but that it was too early to predict earnings for December and the second half of the year.
"We made a modest profit on the Olympics and we look forward to the winter Olympics in Japan about 18 months from now and the summer games in Sydney in the year 2000," he said.
Brown said Prime could not predict when the Australian advertising market would pick up, but that revenues from Prime's operations in Melbourne had improved significantly in the last three months.
Earlier today, Prime said it had agreed to buy the Western Australian-based Golden West Network for A$71 million.

Prime said the deal, which would make Prime Australia's biggest regional television network, would be funded by a A$60 million debt facility from the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd and existing cash reserves.
At 1.10 p.m. (0210 GMT), Prime shares were up seven cents at A$2.45.
